He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio Bobcats]]. After three seasons at Ohio University, Preston was drafted 33rd overall by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2021 NBA draft]] and was traded to the Clippers. He missed his entire rookie season after undergoing surgery to address an injury in his right foot. ==Early life== Preston played basketball for [[William R. Boone High School]] in [[Orlando, Florida]], averaging two points per game over two years.{{cite web |last=Arkley |first=Jason |title=Preston an unlikely freshman standout for Bobcats |url=https://www.athensmessenger.com/sports/ohiouniversity/preston-an-unlikely-freshman-standout-for-bobcats/article_fc8f8079-5695-51d0-a3e7-cc9d4a56d945.html |website=[[The Athens Messenger]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=February 25, 2019}} He stood about {{convert|6|ft|4=2}} tall and weighed {{convert|140|lb}} out of high school and applied to the [[University of Central Florida]] as a regular student, planning to major in [[journalism]]. After competing on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, Preston chose to play basketball at a prep school, joining Believe Prep Academy in [[Athens, Tennessee]].{{cite web |last=Lopresti |first=Mike |title=Keep an eye on Ohio's unheralded Jason Preston, an early star in college basketball 2020 |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2020-11-30/keep-eye-ohios-unheralded-jason-preston-early-star-college-basketball-2020 |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 30, 2020}} He grew {{convert|4|in|cm|spell=in}} and gained experience as a [[point guard]]. Preston averaged 12 points, nine assists and seven rebounds per game, leading his team to a 31–8 record.{{cite web |date=May 15, 2018 |title=Ohio Men's Basketball Adds Preston To 2018-19 Signing Class |url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20180515nsyuao |url-status=dead |access-date=November 27, 2020 |website=Ohio University |archive-date=March 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190307095335/http://ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20180515nsyuao }} He started out playing for the B team and was elevated to the A team after a series of strong performances, but began playing for the C team after receiving little playing time. Preston eventually managed to rejoin the A team. After posting his highlights to [[Twitter]], Preston received college basketball offers from [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio]] and [[Longwood Lancers men's basketball|Longwood]], eventually committing to play for Ohio. ==College career== As a freshman at Ohio University, Preston averaged six points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, earning [[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |title=Jason Preston |url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/bios/preston_jason_pbop |access-date=November 27, 2020 |website=Ohio University}}{{dead link|date=November 2023}} On November 13, 2019, he posted a sophomore season-high 27 points, 14 rebounds and five assists in an 81–72 win over [[2019–20 Iona Gaels men's basketball team|Iona]].{{cite web |title=Preston scores 27 pts to lead Ohio University over Iona 81-72 |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=28075038 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=November 13, 2019}} On January 21, 2020, Preston recorded 27 points, eight assists and seven rebounds in an 83–74 loss to [[2019–20 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]].{{cite web |last=McMillan |first=Lonnie |title=Jackson, Knapke lead Toledo past Ohio University 83-74 |url=https://www.bobcatattack.com/basketball/story.asp?PID=1219 |website=Bobcat Attack |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=January 21, 2020}} On February 8, he scored 15 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists, becoming the second player in program history to register a [[triple-double]], in a 77–46 win over [[2019–20 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami (Ohio)]].{{cite web |last=Poisal |first=Anthony |title=Men's Basketball: Jason Preston's pregame suggestion, triple-double carry Ohio University to blowout win over Miami |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2020/02/ohio-bobcats-mens-basketball-jason-preston-battle-of-the-bricks-miami-redhawks |website=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=February 8, 2020}} As a sophomore, Preston averaged 16.8 points, 7.4 assists and 6.4 rebounds per game and was a Second Team All-MAC selection. He led the MAC and ranked second in the nation in assists.{{cite web |last=Mauro |first=Bryan |title=MAC Basketball: In-depth look at Ohio Bobcats junior guard Jason Preston |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/07/19/mac-basketball-in-depth-look-at-ohio-bobcats-junior-guard-jason-preston/2/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=July 19, 2020}} On November 27, 2020, Preston recorded a career-high 31 points, eight assists and six rebounds in a 77–75 loss to eighth-ranked [[2020–21 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]].{{cite web |last=Werner |first=Jeremy |title=Quick hits: No. 8 Illini survive scare from Ohio 77-75 |url=https://247sports.com/college/illinois/Article/Illinois-basketball-Ohio-Bobcats-recap-quick-hits-155472274/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=November 27, 2020 |date=November 27, 2020}} His story drew national attention following the performance.{{cite web |last=Sykes |first=Mike D. II |date=November 28, 2020 |title=Listen to Ohio guard Jason Preston's absolutely incredible story |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/lists/jason-preston-story-ohio-illinois-guard |access-date=December 1, 2020 |website=For The Win}}{{cite web |last=Colant |first=Juliana |title=OU point guard Jason Preston goes viral over the weekend; Athens County has over 2,000 COVID-19 cases |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2020/11/ohio-university-basketball-player-jason-preston-goes-viral-covid-cases-athens-county |website=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 29, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Gaydos |first=Ryan |title=Ohio University point guard's backstory goes viral as he drops 31 points vs. Illinois |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/ohio-university-point-guard-backstory-viral-illinois |website=[[Fox News]] |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 28, 2020}} On January 23, 2021, he posted his second triple-double, with 11 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds in an 85–77 win against [[2020–21 Ball State Cardinals men's basketball team|Ball State]].{{cite magazine |title=Preston triple-double leads Ohio past Ball St. 85-77 |url=https://www.si.com/college/college-basketball/game/2307724 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=January 23, 2021}} Preston was named [[most valuable player]] of the [[2021 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] after leading Ohio University to the title.{{cite web |last=Kirven |first=J. L. |title=Men's Basketball: Jason Preston and Ben Vander Plas lead Ohio back to the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2021/03/ohio-bobcats-mens-basketball-jason-preston-and-ben-vander-plas-mac-championship |website=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 14, 2021}} On March 20, in the first round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], he helped the 13th-seeded Bobcats to a 62–58 upset victory over fourth-seeded [[2020–21 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], recording 11 points, 13 rebounds and eight assists.{{cite web |last=Marot |first=Michael |title=Virginia loses 62-58 to Preston, Ohio, ending title defense |url=https://apnews.com/article/virginia-cavaliers-mens-basketball-jason-preston-coronavirus-pandemic-virginia-indiana-bb8748c06ff389599f930c676c9815b9 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 21, 2021}} As a junior, Preston averaged 15.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 7.3 assists per game, earning First Team All-MAC honors. On April 26, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Gleckler |first=Jack |date=April 26, 2021 |title=Men's Basketball: Jason Preston declares for the 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.thepostathens.com/article/2021/04/ohio-bobcats-mens-basketball-jason-preston-declare-for-2021-nba-draft |access-date=April 26, 2021 |website=The Post}} He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=July 7, 2021 |title=Ohio Bobcats guard Jason Preston to remain in 2021 NBA draft, sign with agent |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31778557 |access-date=July 26, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}} After beginning his professional NBA career, Preston completed his degree at [[Ohio University]], graduating [[cum laude]] in 2022 with a Bachelor of [[Sport Management]] and a minor in [[Finance]]. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2021–2023)=== Preston was selected with the 33rd overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by his hometown team, the [[Orlando Magic]] and was then traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite news|first=Swanson|last=Mirjam|title=Clippers eager to bet on Ohio's Jason Preston|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2021/07/30/clippers-eager-to-bet-on-ohios-jason-preston/|work=[[The Orange County Register]]|date=July 30, 2021v}} On August 9, 2021, Preston signed a three-year rookie-scale contract with the Clippers.{{cite web|title=Clippers' Jason Preston: Signs rookie contract|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-jason-preston-signs-rookie-contract/|website=CBSSports.com|date=9 August 2021 |access-date=March 27, 2022}} On October 7, 2021, he underwent surgery after suffering an injury on his right foot during the preseason of his rookie campaign.{{cite web|first=Ohm|last=Youngmisuk|title=LA Clippers rookie Jason Preston has right foot surgery|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32356048 |website=ESPN.com|date=October 7, 2021|access-date=November 10, 2021}} Preston missed the entire [[2021–22 NBA season|2021–22 season]] after undergoing surgery. Preston made his NBA debut on October 23, 2022, playing three minutes in a 112–95 loss to the [[2022–23 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|first=Beth|last=Harris|title=SUNS BEAT CLIPS 112-95, PAUL 3RD NBA PLAYER WITH 11K ASSISTS|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200043|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2023}} He played sparingly in the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]], appearing in only 14 games.{{Cite web |title=Jason Preston Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/prestja01.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On October 1, 2023, Preston was waived by the Clippers.{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Kirschenbaum|title=Jason Preston Waived By Clippers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/jason-preston-being-waived-by-clippers.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 1, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} === Memphis Hustle (2023–2024) === On October 16, 2023, Preston signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|title=The @memgrizz today announced the team signed Jason Preston and Timmy Allen.|number=1713902109341409778|user=GrizzliesPR|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=October 16, 2023}} but was waived two days later.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Adonis Arms and David Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-adonis-arms-and-david-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}} On October 30, he joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2023-24 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}} ===Utah Jazz (2024)=== On January 9, 2024, Preston signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Jason Preston to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-jason-preston-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2024|access-date=January 10, 2024}} Preston was waived by the Jazz on November 22 due to a left calf strain injury. Preston appeared in seven games for the Jazz and 26 for the Stars.{{cite web|title= Utah Jazz Sign David Jones to Two-Way Contract |url= https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-david-jones-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2024|access-date=November 22, 2024}} In his time with the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] of the [[NBA G League]], Preston emerged as a dominant guard. In March 2024 he was named the G League Player of the Week after averaging 23.0 points, 12.0 rebounds and 13.0 assists on 54.0 percent shooting during a 3‑0 week. [https://gleague.nba.com/news/jason-preston-named-g-league-player-of-the-week "Jason Preston Named G League Player Of The Week"]. NBA G League. March 12 2024. The following month he earned the Kia NBA G League Player of the Month award for March 2024 after averaging 19.4 points, 11.2 rebounds and 11.8 assists while leading his team on an 11‑game winning streak. [https://gleague.nba.com/news/jason-preston-named-kia-g-league-player-of-the-month "Jason Preston Named Kia G League Player Of The Month"]. NBA G League. April 3 2024. He also earned All‑NBA G League First Team honors for the season. [https://www.slcdunk.com/nba-g-league-salt-lake-city-stars/2024/4/19/24134838/utah-jazz-players-jason-preston-and-kenny-lofton-jr-win-all-nba-g-league-first-team-honors-nba-stars "Utah Jazz players Jason Preston and Kenneth Lofton Jr win All‑NBA G League First Team honors"]. SLC Dunk. April 19 2024. ===San Diego Clippers (2025–present)=== On August 12, 2025, Preston signed a training camp deal with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web |last=Koch |first=Jared |date=August 13, 2025 |title=Former Utah Jazz Guard Signs With Clippers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/news/former-utah-jazz-guard-signs-with-los-angeles-clippers-jason-preston |access-date=August 22, 2025 |website=SI.com |language=en}} However on October 18, Preston was waived by the Clippers.{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Luke |date=October 1, 2025 |title=Clippers Waive Jason Preston |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/jason-preston-being-waived-by-clippers.html |access-date=October 20, 2025 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en}}{{cite web | last=Simon | first=Dean | title=Clippers officially waive 6-foot-9 ex-Warriors forward, G-League superstar guard | website=Yahoo! His father was absent from his life. After his mother's death, Preston's aunt and uncle, who were living in [[Jamaica]], became his [[legal guardian]]s, though he remained in the United States and lived with the son of his mother's friend. He grew up watching the [[Detroit Pistons]] and has written about the team for online publications. In April 2023, he was featured as the subject of an [[AT&T]] commercial that chronicled some unfortunate events in his early life. He had produced a highlight video that helped earn him a Division I scholarship with Ohio and an eventual pro career.{{cite web |date=April 4, 2023 |title=WATCH: VIRAL VIDEO OF JASON PRESTON SECURED CLIPPERS POINT GUARD SPOT AT COLLEGE |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2023/04/04/watch-viral-video-of-jason-preston-secured-clippers-point-guard-spot-at-college/ |access-date=April 5, 2023 |website=hitc.com |archive-date=April 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405180500/https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2023/04/04/watch-viral-video-of-jason-preston-secured-clippers-point-guard-spot-at-college/ |url-status=dead }} Preston married college sweetheart Micaylah Nash (now Micaylah Preston) in July 2024 at an intimate destination wedding at [[Round Hill Hotel and Villas]] in Montego Bay, Jamaica, attended by 60 guests and covered by The Knot.[https://www.theknot.com/content/jason-preston-wedding "Exclusive: Inside NBA Player Jason Preston’s Jamaica Destination Wedding"]. *The Knot*. July 24, 2024. In lieu of wedding gifts, the couple requested donations to the American Lung Association to honor Preston’s late mother.[https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/professional-basketball-player-jason-preston-joins-american-lung-association-ambassador-council-to-honor-mother-301998195.html “Professional Basketball Player Jason Preston Joins American Lung Association Ambassador Council to Honor Mother.” PR Newswire. November 27, 2023.] Preston’s family still resides in Jamaica, as his late mother was born and raised there. Beyond his on-court career, Preston has established a presence as a basketball educator and content creator. He regularly posts tutorial videos on YouTube and social media platforms, breaking down game film, dribbling techniques, and point-guard decision-making from an NBA-player perspective. His content is designed to give free access to training and insight, particularly to young athletes who may lack resources.{{cite web |title=How Jason Preston Is Giving the Keys to the Next Generation |url=https://slamonline.com/nba/jason-preston-259/ |website=SLAM |date=November 6, 2025 |access-date=November 12, 2025}} In 2025, Preston appeared on the game show Family Feud.{{Cite web |last=Anders |first=Andy |date=April 29, 2025 |title=Buckeye Walk-On Braylen Nash, Family to Appear On 'Family Feud' |url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball/2025/04/156030/buckeye-walk-on-braylen-nash-family-to-appear-on-family-feud}} He appeared with his wife's family, which included his brother in-law Braylen who played basketball at Ohio State. The family won prize money on the show in the Fast Money round.{{Cite web |last=Jardy |first=Adam |date=March 15, 2025 |title=New Albany's Nash family, including Ohio State's Braylen, wins 'Family Feud' grand prize |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2025/05/15/family-feud-ohio-state-braylen-nash-family-new-albany-wins-grand-prize/83642882007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z115732p119350n00----c00----e1164xxv115732d--43--b--43--&gca-ft=183&gca-ds=sophi}} The team, the Nash family, won the $20,000 on the 2nd day they appeared. The tam also won another $20,000 on their 3rd appearance day.{{Cite web |last=Engels |first=Patrick |date=May 17, 2025 |title=Ohio State Walk-On Guard Braylen Nash Appears On “Family Feud,” Family Wins Over $40,000 |url=https://buckeyesports.com/ohio-state-walk-on-guard-braylen-nash-appears-on-family-feud-family-wins-over-40000/}} The Nash family hailed from New Albany, Ohio. ==Philanthropy== After losing his mother to lung cancer from second-hand smoke, Preston has made it his mission to raise awareness about lung cancer and early detection. He serves as an ambassador for the [[American Lung Association]]. [https://www.lung.org/about-us/ambassador-council/jason-preston “Jason Preston | American Lung Association Ambassador Council”]. American Lung Association. Retrieved November 2025. Since 2022, Preston has partnered with his alma mater, Ohio University, annually for Lung Cancer Awareness Month. He has provided white shoes for the basketball team, the color representing lung cancer awareness, shared custom T-shirts featuring his mother’s name, and helped produce public service announcements (PSAs) to educate about lung cancer prevention and early detection. [https://www.si.com/nba/clippers/onsi/news/jason-preston-honoring-mother-during-lung-cancer-awareness-month “Jason Preston Honoring Mother During Lung Cancer Awareness Month”]. Sports Illustrated. Retrieved November 2025. In 2022, while with the Los Angeles Clippers, he honored his late mother by wearing specially designed “KD Aunt Pearl” shoes in all games and practices. In 2023, he joined the American Lung Association’s Ambassador Council to further advocate for lung health and honor his mother’s memory. [https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/professional-basketball-player-jason-preston-joins-american-lung-association-ambassador-council-to-honor-mother-301998195.html “Professional Basketball Player Jason Preston Joins American Lung Association Ambassador Council to Honor Mother.” PR Newswire. November 27 2023. Preston and his wife also requested donations to the [[American Lung Association]] in lieu of wedding gifts, aligning his personal milestone with his philanthropic mission.
